title: Artemisinin-based combination therapies against artemether-lumefantrine: three direct comparisons, a network with no closed loop, and no indirect estimate
question: Among trials comparing an artemisinin-based combination therapy with artemether-lumefantrine, what is the PCR-corrected treatment failure in each direct comparison, and can the resulting network support an indirect comparison between the therapies that were never randomised against each other?
_prose_rule: Prose may not restate a number the object holds structurally.
_sourcing_rule: Every MEASURED input carries the verbatim sentence it was read from. Where a paper reports adequate responses and this object stores failures, the subtraction is shown in the staged extract.
_estimand_rule: The outcome is a proportion of evaluable participants, so counts are the correct storage form. Each comparison is its own outcome, because the interventions differ and combining them would average across drugs.
completeness_statement: Every registration that contributes data is held and reported. Nothing was cited and then dropped, so there is no removal block. Two further eligible registrations post no results; they are listed under eligible_but_not_contributing and are not excluded.

eligible_but_not_contributing.note: These registrations meet the eligibility criteria and are NOT excluded. They contribute no data because neither posts results. The Handbook section governing the selection process sends a completed but unreported study that clearly meets the criteria to the included side rather than out of the review, and forbids omitting a study solely because its outcome data are unreported; that section is cited on the scope decision.

network.multi_arm_covariance_note: The schema carries a covariance term for a study contributing more than one contrast against a shared arm, because a network must. NO included study is multi-arm, so the term is not exercised here and no covariance is estimated. Recording that it is unexercised is the point: a facility that has never run is not evidence that it works.
network.status: exploratory only; not a robust network meta-analysis
network.why_no_network_estimate: An indirect comparison between two treatments never randomised against each other IS constructible here: they meet at a common comparator, which is what Handbook section 11.2.1 describes, and a star graph supplies that path even though it contains no closed loop. An earlier version of this object said the absence of a loop meant there was no path at all, which is wrong, and a reviewer was right to say so. What the absence of a loop actually costs is the CHECK: section 11.4.4 assesses disagreement between evidence sources, and 11.4.4.1 measures incoherence in a closed loop as the absolute difference between the direct and the indirect summary estimate. With no loop there is no such difference to compute, so the assumption that indirect and direct evidence agree cannot be tested at all here. NO INDIRECT ESTIMATE IS COMPUTED, and the reason is a judgement about TRANSITIVITY under 11.2.2 rather than a graph-theoretic impossibility: that section requires the sets of trials to be similar, on average, in all important factors other than the comparison being made, and these are not. Every edge meets the same comparator, so the graph is joined; what differs is WHEN the outcome was measured, one comparison ending its follow-up a fortnight later than the other two. One trial dosed at home rather than under observation, making it a measurement of effectiveness where the others measure efficacy. Those are the grounds, and they are differences in effect modifiers, which is what that section is about. That each comparison rests on one study is ALSO true and is NOT part of this ground: it is a limit on precision and on replication, not an effect modifier, and an earlier version wrongly folded it in. The missing loop is why the judgement cannot be checked rather than why it holds.

methodological_authority.reference: Higgins JPT, Thomas J, Chandler J, Cumpston M, Li T, Page MJ, et al (editors). Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1. Cochrane, 2025.
methodological_authority.version_checked_how: The publisher's own page for each chapter relied on was opened and its printed citation line read. The version and the dates below are what those lines say, not what an earlier build of this object assumed. The publisher's versions-and-changes page was read on the same day and is what settles which version is current: it lists 6.5.1 as the newest release line, with entries dated 2026 and 2025, above 6.5 dated 2024. Two of the publisher's own pages disagree with that and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved: the Handbook landing page and the current-version index both still print version 6.5 updated August 2024. Where they conflict this object follows the version history and the per-chapter citation lines, because those are the more specific and the more recent statements, and the newest release listed under 6.5.1 revised a chapter this object does not cite.
methodological_authority.version_note: The Handbook is versioned as a whole AND dated per chapter, and the two do not move together: the table above gives each chapter the version and the last-updated date the publisher prints on it, and they are not the same as each other. An earlier version of this object named one version and one update month for the whole Handbook, and that pair matched neither the current version nor any date printed on the chapters actually relied on. Listing them chapter by chapter keeps the age of the authority behind each decision visible instead of averaged away; one of these chapters is a good deal older than the others.

asaq_vs_al.analysed_scope: the per-protocol evaluable participants at day 28. The paper reports cure percentages rather than counts, and these denominators are the ones those percentages resolve to.

source_quotes: The PP PCR adjusted day 28 cure rates were [AS-AQ = 96.9% (95% CI, 91.2-99.4) versus AL = 95.5% (95% CI, 89.9-98.5), P = 0.797].
A cure rate of 96.9 per cent corresponds to 94 of 97 evaluable, that is 3 failures of 97; a cure rate of 95.5 per cent corresponds to 107 of 112, that is 5 failures of 112.
After the first dose, antimalarial drugs were given at home, rather than under direct observation by a study staff.
provenance.quote_note: The second quote is why this trial is not interchangeable with the other two: its doses were taken at home rather than observed, so it measures effectiveness where they measure efficacy.

handbook.decision: Report the three direct comparisons and compute NO indirect or mixed estimate, on a TRANSITIVITY judgement rather than on the shape of the graph; and On the row whose treatment arm recorded no failures, store the boundary point estimate and NO interval, and add no constant to any cell
handbook.conformance: Section 11.2.1 defines the indirect comparison a common comparator makes available, so the path exists and the decision not to use it is a choice that must be argued. Section 11.2.2 supplies the argument: transitivity requires the sets of trials to be similar, on average, in all important factors other than the comparison being made, and here they differ in when the outcome was measured and in whether dosing was observed. Both are effect modifiers, which is what that section asks about. That each comparison rests on one study is not offered as a transitivity ground, because it is not one. Sections 11.4.4 and 11.4.4.1 are why the judgement cannot be checked: incoherence is measured in a closed loop as the difference between direct and indirect estimates, and this graph has none. Section 10.4.4.1 is the case of a study with no events in one or more arms. Section 10.4.4 records that software routines add a fixed value, typically one half, to all cells of a two-by-two table where the problem occurs, and that doing so 'usually has the undesirable effect of biasing study estimates towards no difference and over-estimating variances of study estimates'. The correction exists to let a study enter a pooled estimate. This row enters none, so the correction would buy an interval and no comparison, and it is not applied.

per_trial.not_log_transformable_because: The stored point is a boundary value. Zero has no logarithm, so the log-scale normal approximation that supplies every other interval in this object cannot supply one here.
per_trial.interval_absent_reason: An interval on this row would require adding a constant to each cell, and Cochrane Handbook section 10.4.4 warns that correction 'usually has the undesirable effect of biasing study estimates towards no difference'. Section 10.4.4.1 is the specific case, a study with no events in an arm. Nothing on this row is pooled with anything, so adding the constant would buy an interval and no comparison. The counts are what the trial reports and they are shown.
per_trial.derivation: risk ratio of PCR-corrected treatment failure, computed from this trial's own two-by-two counts. The treatment arm recorded no failures at all, so the ratio takes the smallest value it can take. Failure is the outcome, so that is the best direction, not a missing result.

SCOPE:awaiting-results-registrations.decision: Record two completed registrations as ELIGIBLE BUT CONTRIBUTING NO DATA, awaiting results; do not treat them as excluded
SCOPE:awaiting-results-registrations.conformance: Section 4.3.3 covers trials registers as a source to be searched, and both registrations were retrieved there; neither carries a results section. Section 4.6.3 governs the DISPOSITION, and it has now been read rather than named. Its selection process ends by asking the reviewer to tag or record any completed or terminated study not yet reported so that it goes to either the included studies table or the table of studies awaiting classification, the choice between the two turning on whether the study clearly meets the eligibility criteria; the same section adds that a study should not be omitted from a review solely because measured outcome data are not reported, and the MECIR expectation printed beside it makes not excluding on that ground mandatory. Both registrations are completed, both are unreported, and both clearly meet the eligibility criteria, so the disposition the section directs is the included side of that choice, carrying no data. That is what this object records. Earlier rounds of this object had the citation wrong in both directions and both are withdrawn: 4.6.5 governs studies listed as EXCLUDED, which these are not, and before that a passage about reports in unreadable languages was cited on the strength of an analogy, which is not conformance. This build previously named 4.6.3 as UNREAD, because five retrievals truncated before it; the truncation was in the retrieval, not the source, and fetching the chapter's own bytes rather than a summary of them returned the section in full.
